title: How did people tell time before modern clocks?
sources: Smithsonian Clocks and Watches Historical Survey

lines.text: Before wristwatches and smartphones existed, how did ancient humans know what time it was?
lines.caps: How did people *tell time | before clocks existed?

lines.text: Ancient Egyptians tracked shadows cast by giant stone obelisks, creating the world's first sundials.
lines.caps: Egyptians used stone *obelisks | as giant solar *sundials

lines.text: On cloudy days and at night, Greeks and Romans relied on water clocks called clepsydras.
Water dripped steadily out of a calibrated stone vessel, marking passing hours on internal indicator lines.
lines.caps: Dripping water marked *passing hours | like an hourglass!

lines.text: In ancient China, people burned incense coils with small brass weights that clattered into copper bowls every hour.
Monasteries eventually built mechanical pendulum and gear clocktowers to chime daily prayer bells.
Measuring time transformed humanity from wandering hunter-gatherers into coordinated industrial civilizations.
